definitions.type: compact additive group with normalized measure
definitions.definition: torus=ℝ/(2πℤ), written \mathbb T in formulas; integration uses dx/(2π). The parameter T denotes the time horizon.

definitions.type: Fourier coefficient map on the torus
definitions.definition: For integrable f, Fourier(f)(k) = fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^{2 pi} f(x) exp(-ikx) dx; extend by distributional duality.

For real s, H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with norm squared sum_{k in Z} <k>^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are distributions. L2=H^0 with normalized measure. On mean-zero distributions dot H^s has squared norm sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2. Smooth means spatially C-infinity. Real means fhat(-k)=conjugate(fhat(k)), and mean-zero means fhat(0)=0. Sequence ell2 uses counting measure. Time L-infinity norms are essential suprema, except time suprema of continuous representatives. Generic constants C may change; C_M depends only on gamma,T,M, never on a Fourier support bound or timestep.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real times
definitions.definition: S_t = exp(-t partial_x^3); Fourier(S_t f)(k)= exp(it k^3) fhat(k).
P0 f=fhat(0), as a constant function.
P=I-P0; the identity operator is I.

definitions.type: inverse spatial derivative with zero mode removed
definitions.definition: Dinv=partial_x^(-1)=D^(-1), Fourier multiplier (ik)^(-1) at nonzero k and zero at k=0.
Dinv2=D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv.

definitions.type: quadratic increment, for positive tau and L2 inputs
definitions.definition: F_\tau(f)&=\tfrac16 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)^2]-\tfrac16 S_\tau P[(D^{-1}f)^2],\\

definitions.type: cubic increment, for positive tau and L2 inputs
definitions.definition:
H_\tau(f)&=\tfrac13 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)D^{-1}F_\tau(f)]
+\tfrac{\tau}{9}(S_\tau D^{-1}f)P_0(f^2)\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{54}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-1}[(S_sD^{-1}f)^3]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{27\tau}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-2}[(S_{s-\tau}D^{-2}F_\tau(f))(S_sD^{-1}f)]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}.

definitions.type: one-step update and its finite iterates
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f) for tau>0. For any initial datum g0 and positive integer L with tau=T/L, set t_n=n tau, u_{g0}^0=g0, u_{g0}^{n+1}=Psi_tau(u_{g0}^n) for 0<=n<L, and v_{g0}^n=S_{-t_n}u_{g0}^n. Suppress the subscript g0 for the datum under discussion, using g0=u0 in the target. There is no spatial projection in Psi.
M_tau(g)=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds for tau>0.

\eta_\tau(\alpha,\beta)=M_\tau(e^{-is(\alpha+\beta)})
-M_\tau(e^{-is\alpha})M_\tau(e^{-is\beta}).

definitions.type: averaged cubic remainder on mean-zero polynomials, subsequently extended
definitions.definition: R2 = R^n_{2,tau}. For tau>0, real t_n and mean-zero polynomial f1,f2,f3, its output at k=0 is zero, and at k!=0 is -tau/(18 i k) sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0} exp(-i t_n Phi) eta_tau(alpha,beta) f1hat(a) f2hat(b) f3hat(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3abp, beta=3kcp, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The polynomial definition grants no bounded extension; a bounded extension must be proved separately.
B_t(f,g)=mathcal B_t(f,g)=S_{-t} partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)].
J_t(f,g)=mathcal J_t(f,g)=S_{-t}P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

definitions.type: time-integrated trilinear operator initially on smooth inputs
definitions.definition: C_I(f,g,h)= integral_I S_{-t}P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)](S_t Dinv h)} dt. For lower regularity its meaning is the bounded extension supplied by the continuous estimates.

For compact interval I, ||f||_{X(I)}=||f||_{L-infinity(I;L2)}+||partial_t f||_{L-infinity(I;H^(-pstar))}, using the distributional time derivative. Subintervals use the same continuous representatives; piecewise smooth continuous functions have this distributional derivative almost everywhere.
a_gamma=1/2-gamma if 0<gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 if 1/2<gamma<=1.
For time-independent mean-zero f and t in I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], F_n(t;f)=1/2 integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f,f) ds. Write F_n(t)=F_n(t;f) when f is fixed.
z_n(t)=f+F_n(t;f).
C_n(t;f)=integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f,F_n(s;f)) ds.
Q_n(t;f)=1/2 integral_{t_n}^t B_s(F_n(s;f),F_n(s;f)) ds.
W_n(f)=Q_n(t_n+tau;f)+R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f).

definitions.type: piecewise numerical interpolation, initially for smooth data
definitions.definition: For any smooth mean-zero step input f, time t_n and tau>0, define the step interpolation V(t;f)=f+F_n(t;f)+C_n(t;f)+Q_n(t;f)-(t-t_n)W_n(f)/tau on [t_n,t_n+tau]. On a numerical trajectory write V(t)=V(t;v^n) with f=v^n on I_n. Agreement of adjacent pieces is a proved property, not part of the definition.
For a step input f, Y_n(t;f)=V(t;f)-z_n(t;f); along a trajectory take f=v^n and suppress the input.

\rho_n(t)=-\int_{t_n}^t\mathcal B_s(Y_n,z_n)\,ds
-\tfrac12\int_{t_n}^t\mathcal B_s(Y_n,Y_n)\,ds
-\frac{t-t_n}{\tau}W_n.
Res=mathcal R, Res(0)=0 and Res(t)=sum_{j<n}rho_j(t_{j+1})+rho_n(t) on I_n, with the stage input f=v^j in each increment.

inputs.statement: There is a finite A(T,gamma,R) uniform for every real mean-zero datum g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R. Its KdV equation u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=g, has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation, solving the equation distributionally, with sup_t||u(t)||_{H^gamma}<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions. For v(t)=S_{-t}u(t), v'=B_t(v,v)/2 and all Sobolev norms of v and u agree. For two such exact flows with initial L2 norms summing to at most B0, sup_t||u-tilde u||_2<=C(T,B0)||g-tilde g||_2. In particular M=1+sup_t||v(t)||_{H^gamma}<=1+A uniformly.

For every I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1, and fj in X(I), ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X+C||fi||_{L-infinity H^(-pstar)} product_{j!=i}||fj||_{L-infinity L2}, each i=1,2,3. For time-independent fj in H^lambda, 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}. At a=b the integral is zero. These are bounded extensions from smooth inputs and apply to continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs. For mean-zero w with ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M and 0<tau<=1, sup_{I_n}||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C_M tau^gamma and sup_{I_n}||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{1+gamma}}<=C_M. Also ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_{H^gamma}||g||_{H^{a_gamma}}. Constants are uniform in step location and Fourier support.

For all real t and mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Dinv f||_{H^1}+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_{H^1}<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. For L2 F,G, ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A with Dinv A in L2, ||A||_{H^(-pstar)}<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 is an algebra with product norm <=C product of norms. S_t is a Sobolev isometry preserving reality and mean. Projections P_{<=N}, P_{>N} contract Sobolev norms and X, and for s>=s0,N>=1, ||P_{>N}f||_{H^{s0}}<=C N^(s0-s)||f||_{H^s}, ||P_{<=N}f||_{H^s}<=C N^(s-s0)||f||_{H^{s0}}. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). The identities hold for continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs by summing pieces.

inputs.statement: For any smooth real mean-zero initial datum g0, with all iterates initialized by g0, and positive integer L with tau=T/L>0, scheme iterates are smooth real and mean-zero. V is continuous on [0,T], spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth, and V(t_n)=v^n=S_{-t_n}u^n. On every step f=v^n, v^{n+1}=f+F_n(t_{n+1})+C_n(t_{n+1})-R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f). Moreover F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2, V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau, Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau, and Y_n(t_n)=0.

For smooth mean-zero f,w on I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1, ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, delta_n=||f-w||_2<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n, form F_n,z_n,C_n,Q_n,W_n,V,Y_n by the step formulas with input f. Uniformly on I_n, ||F_n||_{H^1}<=C_M, ||F_n-F_n(.;w)||_{H^1}<=C_M delta_n, ||F_n||_{H^{a_gamma}}+||F_n||_2<=C_M q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M; ||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q_n and sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n; sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M q_n; sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q_n; sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M q_n, ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n and sup||Y_n||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C_M tau q_n. Exactly C_n(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F_n(t))-(1/6)C_[t_n,t](f,f,f). No numerical Sobolev bound is required.

For any smooth numerical trajectory, Res is continuous piecewise smooth, Res(0)=0, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Res', and on each step Res'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. When comparison w=v(t_n) has H^gamma norm <=M, delta_n=||v^n-w||_2<=1, 0<tau<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n, sup_{I_n}||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and ||Res'||_{L-infinity(I_n;H^(-pstar))}<=C_M q_n. These estimates include every partial step endpoint.

output.statement: For every smooth real mean-zero initial datum g0 with ||g0||_{H^gamma}<=R, using its exact and numerical flows, let v be the exact twisted solution, M=1+sup_t||v(t)||_{H^gamma}, e=v-V, and let I=[a,b] subset [0,T] start at a grid point, with h=b-a<=1 and step 0<tau<=1. If E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, then sup_I||Res(t)-Res(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_X+||V||_X<=C_M. For every N>=2, E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Constants are uniform in data with this bound M, step and support. The endpoint b may be inside a step.

argument.text: Use H001 and an arbitrary smooth real mean-zero datum g0 with ||g0||_{H^gamma}<=R. N001 gives its smooth exact twisted flow v and M. N007 gives continuous V agreeing with the numerical grid. Put e=v-V, I=[a,b] subset [0,T], h=b-a<=1, starting at a grid point. Assume L1: 0<tau<=1 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. Every intersected step has delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. Summing the N009 increment bound over at most h/tau+1 steps gives sup_I||Res(t)-Res(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). The exact derivative identity is e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Res'. Apply N006 and N009 to get ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I). Also ||V||_2<=||v||_2+1 and V'=B(V,V)/2+Res' give ||v||_X+||V||_X<=C_M. Continuity permits these statements across step interfaces.

For any \(t\in I\), define \(\mathcal F_I(t)=\int_a^t\mathcal B_s(e,v-e/2)\,ds\). The exact error identity is
\[
e(t)=e(a)+\mathcal F_I(t)-(\mathcal R(t)-\mathcal R(a)). 
\]
Choose a Fourier threshold \(N\ge2\) only in the proof. It is not part of the algorithm. The low frequencies satisfy
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{\le N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_MN^2hE_I. 
\]
For example \(\|\partial_x^{-1}P(fg)\|_{L^2}\lesssim\|f\|_{L^2}\|g\|_{L^2}\), followed by the two-derivative Bernstein bound, proves the low-frequency estimate.

For high frequencies, the normal-form identity N006 gives, retaining *both* endpoints,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal F_I(t)
&=\tfrac13[\mathcal J_s(e,v-e/2)]_{s=a}^{s=t}
-\tfrac13C_{[a,t]}(e,v-e/2,V)-\tfrac16C_{[a,t]}(v,v,e)\\
&\quad+\tfrac13\int_a^t\mathcal J_s(\mathcal R',V)\,ds. 
\end{aligned}
\]
For an explicit verification put \(g=v-e/2\). Then \(e'=\mathcal B(e,g)-\mathcal R'\) and \(g'=\tfrac12\mathcal B(v,v)-\tfrac12\mathcal B(e,g)+\tfrac12\mathcal R'\).
In the differentiated terms of the normal-form identity N006, symmetry of \(\mathcal J\) gives \(C(e,g,g)-\tfrac12C(e,g,e)=C(e,g,V)\) because \(g-e/2=V\).
The remaining cubic term is \(\tfrac12C(v,v,e)\), and the forcing terms are
\(-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',g)+\tfrac12\mathcal J(e,\mathcal R')=-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',V)\).
Multiplication by \(-1/3\) yields exactly the normal-form expansion. The endpoint terms after \(P_{>N}\) are bounded by \(C_MN^{-1}E_I\) by the \(H^1\) bound for \(\mathcal J\) in the elementary bounds N006.
Here P_{<=N} denotes the multiplier 1_{|k|<=N}; its complement is P_{>N}. The low estimate uses N006's Dinv P product bound and the factor k^2<=N^2. F001 gives the differentiated equations, and N006 justifies the normal form piecewise: continuous interface endpoints cancel. The initial endpoint at a is retained even when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: With mathcal F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds, e(t)=e(a)+mathcal F_I(t)-(Res(t)-Res(a)) and sup||P_{<=N}mathcal F_I||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I. Exactly mathcal F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)C_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)C_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Res',V)ds. The high-output boundary terms are <=C_M N^(-1)E_I.

argument.text:
We spell out how the high-output trilinear terms are estimated. If all three inputs have frequencies at most \(N/3\), the output cannot exceed \(N\). Write \(Lo=P_{\le N/3}\) and \(Hi=Id-Lo\). Here Id denotes the identity operator. The telescoping expansion is
\(C(f_1,f_2,f_3)-C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Lof_3)=C(Hif_1,f_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Hif_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Hif_3)\).
The low-input term has no output above \(N\), and each projection contracts both components of \(X(I)\). For the specified high input, \(\|Hif_i\|_{H^{-p_*}}\le CN^{-p_*}\|f_i\|_2\). In the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, place the \(H^{-p_*}\) norm on that input. Bernstein gives
\[
\|P_{>N}C_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)\|_{L^2}
\le Ch\prod_j\|f_j\|_{X(I)}+CN^{-p_*}\prod_j\|f_j\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2)}. 
\]
Applying F001 to the two cubic terms in the normal-form identity F002 yields \(C_Mh\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+N^{-p_*})E_I\).

The forcing integral in F002 requires the stepwise formula for \(\mathcal R'\) in the residual identity N009. On each intersected step it becomes a sum of
\[
-C(Y_n,z_n,V),\qquad-\tfrac12C(Y_n,Y_n,V),\qquad
-\tau^{-1}\int\mathcal J_s(W_n,V)\,ds.
\]
The first two are \(O(\tau q_n)\) by the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, with the negative norm on \(Y_n\), and N008, F001. The last is \(O(\tau q_n)\) by N008 and the \(L^2\) bound for \(\mathcal J\). Even for a partial final step this is a valid upper bound. Summing gives \(C_M(h+\tau)(\tau^\gamma+E_I)\). Combining these facts,
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{>N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}
\le C_M(h+\tau)\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+\tau+N^{-1}+N^{-p_*})E_I. 
\]
The projection names here are Lo=P_{<=N/3} and Hi=Id-Lo. By N006 they commute with time derivatives and contract X. The middle two normal-form terms each contain e once, hence their products of L2 norms contribute E_I and products of X norms contribute tau^gamma+E_I, by F001. N005 applies with any selected high input in its negative-norm slot. In the forcing integrals use the stepwise identity N009, the two Y_n norms in N008 and the bounds on V in F001. The O(tau q_n) sum includes a possible partial last step.

produces.statement: sup_{t in I}||P_{>N}mathcal F_I(t)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I, including both endpoints and the forcing contribution.

argument.text: Combine the identity and low estimate F002, the high estimate F003 and the residual bound F001. The triangle inequality and time supremum give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I for every N>=2. Discharge L1, preserving its assumptions in the antecedent, and quantify the interval and threshold to get all clauses of the output.
